7.	Abraham Gesner was a Canadian physician turned geologist who, while conducting geological surveys of New Brunswick in the 1840s, became fascinated by the combustion properties of natural bitumen deposits. In 1846, he gave a public demonstration in Charlottetown, Prince Edward Island of a new lamp fuel he had distilled from coal and bituminous rock. The fuel burned more cleanly, more brightly, and more safely than the whale oil or animal fat that most households then relied on for light. He patented his distillation process in the United States in 1854. He named the product X combining the Greek words for wax and oil. His invention came at a critical moment — whale populations were being decimated by the global demand for lamp oil, and X offered a vastly cheaper and more scalable alternative. Gesner has been called the father of the petroleum industry, though he died in relative obscurity in 1864, having sold his patents and seen others profit enormously from his work. Y's Standard Oil would later build much of its early empire on the commercial distribution of X. ID X (10 points) and Y (5 points).
